tools.name: create_draft
tools.title: Create draft email
tools.description:
Creates a new draft email in the authenticated user's Gmail account.

This tool takes recipient addresses (`to`, `cc`, `bcc`), a `subject`, and body content as inputs. Plain text body content can be provided in `body` (do NOT format `body` with Markdown), and rich-text HTML content can be provided in `htmlBody` (use valid HTML tags for formatting; if both are provided, `body` serves as the plain-text alternative). If the draft is created as a reply to an existing message, the ID of the original message should be passed to the tool in the `replyToMessageId` field. Set `includeSignature` to true to append the user's configured Gmail web signature to the draft.

Returns a Draft object with the `id`, `threadId`, and `viewUrl` fields populated.

Attachment.description: Represents an attachment to be included in an email.

content.description: Required. The base64-encoded content of the attachment.

filename.description: Optional. The name of the file to be attached, e.g. "invoice.pdf". Email clients show this name to recipients for both regular and inline attachments. If not provided, the attachment may be received with no name.

id.description: Optional. Output only. When present, contains the ID of an external attachment that can be retrieved in a separate `GetMessageAttachment` request.

inline.description: Optional. If `true`, this attachment is handled as inline. An inline attachment is content, such as an image, that is displayed within the body of an HTML email instead of being listed as a separate file for download. To display an inline attachment, add an `img` element to `htmlBody` whose `src` is `cid:attN`, where N is the attachment's zero-based position in `attachments`, counting all attachments. For example, if `attachments` contains a PDF followed by an inline PNG, set `src="cid:att1"` on the PNG's `img` element. Don't reference inline attachments by `filename`. Other images in `htmlBody` are removed. If `false` or absent, defaults to `false`, and it's treated as a regular attachment.

mimeType.description: Optional. The field representing a content or media type must use IANA MIME type, https://www.iana.org/assignments/media-types/media-types.xhtml. If not provided, defaults to "application/octet-stream".

attachments.description: Optional. The attachments to include in the email. The combined size of attachments in the message cannot exceed 25MB. If you need to send files larger than 25MB, upload the file to Drive first and then insert the Drive link into `body` or `htmlBody`.

bcc.description: Optional. The blind carbon copy recipients of the email draft. Each string MUST be a valid plain email address (e.g., "user@example.com").

body.description: Optional. The plain text body content of the email draft. Do NOT format this field with Markdown (such as headers `#`, bold `**`, bullet points `*`, or tables `|`). If formatted rich text is desired, use `htmlBody` instead. If `htmlBody` is also provided, this field is treated as the plain-text alternative.

cc.description: Optional. The carbon copy recipients of the email draft. Each string MUST be a valid plain email address (e.g., "user@example.com").

htmlBody.description: Optional. The HTML content of the email draft. If provided, this will be used as the rich-text version of the email. Use this field (with valid HTML tags such as `p`, `b`, `ul`, `li`, `h1`) whenever rich text formatting is needed.

includeSignature.description: Optional. Whether to append the user's configured Gmail web signature to the draft. Defaults to false.

replyToMessageId.description: Optional. The ID of the message to reply to. If provided, this will be used as the reply-to message ID for the email draft, and the `body` and `htmlBody` will be appended to the original message body.

subject.description: Optional. The subject line of the email. Defaults to empty if not provided.

to.description: Optional. The primary recipients of the email draft. Each string MUST be a valid plain email address (e.g., "user@example.com").

tools.name: list_drafts
tools.title: List draft emails
tools.description:
Lists draft emails from the authenticated user's Gmail account, optionally filtered by a query string.

Note: An empty JSON object `{}` represents zero matching items, not an error.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of drafts to return. If unspecified, defaults to 20. The maximum allowed value is 50.

pageToken.description: Optional. A token received from a previous `list_drafts` call to retrieve the next page of results. Leave empty to fetch the first page. This is primarily used for pagination to continue fetching results from where the previous `ListDraft` call left off, especially when the number of drafts matching the query exceeds the `pageSize` limit.

query.description: Optional. A query string to filter the drafts. Natural language queries must be pre-converted into Gmail compatible syntax queries to use this tool. If omitted, all drafts (excluding spam and trash by default) are listed. The tool inherently only searches for drafts. Supported Operators by Category: Sender & Recipient: - `from:EMAIL` - Sent from a specific person. - `to:EMAIL` - Sent to a specific person. - `cc:EMAIL` - Specific people in Cc. - `bcc:EMAIL` - Specific people in Bcc. - `deliveredto:EMAIL` - Delivered to a specific address. - `list:EMAIL` - From a specific mailing list. Time & Date: - `after:YYYY/MM/DD` / `newer:YYYY/MM/DD` - Received after a date (evaluates against midnight 00:00:00 of that day, inclusive). - `before:YYYY/MM/DD` / `older:YYYY/MM/DD` - Received before a date (evaluates against midnight 00:00:00 of that day, exclusive; excludes that day). To search through a specific day D (or for a single day D), set `before:` to the day after (for example, `after:2026/02/01 before:2026/02/02` for Feb 1, or `after:2026/02/01 before:2026/02/06` for Feb 1-5). - `older_than:DURATION` - Older than a duration (for example, `1y`, `2d`). - `newer_than:DURATION` - Newer than a duration. Content: - `subject:WORDS` - Words in the subject line. - `has:TYPE` - Has specific content types (attachment, drive, youtube, document). - `filename:NAME` - Attachment with a specific name or type. - `"PHRASE"` - Search for an exact word or phrase. (for example, `"holiday"`, `"holiday vacation"`). - `+WORD` - Match a word exactly. (for example, `+holiday`, `+unicorn`) - `rfc822msgid:ID` - Specific message ID header. - `AROUND N` - Find words near each other (for example, `holiday AROUND 10 vacation`). Labels & Categories: - `label:NAME` - Under a specific label, matched by its display name (the `name` from `list_labels`), for example `label:wins`. Label IDs such as `Label_123` match nothing. Quote a name that contains spaces (`label:"Board Prep"`) or replace its spaces and `/` with `-` (`label:board-prep`). - `category:NAME` - In a category (primary, social, promotions, updates, forums, reservations, purchases). - `in:LABEL` - Search in specific labels (archive, snoozed, trash, sent, inbox, important, starred). For example, `in:trash`, `in:inbox`. Note: Drafts, archived, and sent messages are included by default; use `-in:draft`, `-in:archive`, and `-in:sent` to exclude them. Use `in:inbox` to restrict search to the inbox only. - `has:userlabels` - Has any user labels. - `has:nouserlabels` - Does not have any user labels. - `has:*-star` - Specific star colors (if enabled, for example, `has:yellow-star`). Status: - `is:STATUS` - Search by status (important, starred, unread, read, muted). Size: - `size:BYTES` - Specific size in bytes. - `larger:SIZE` / `smaller:SIZE` - Larger or smaller than a size (for example, `10M` for 10 MB). Logic & Grouping: - `AND` - Match all criteria (default behavior). - `OR` or `{ }` - Match one or more criteria (for example, `from:amy OR from:david`, `{from:amy from:david}`). - `-` (minus) - Exclude criteria (for example, `-movie`). - `( )` - Group multiple search terms (for example, `subject:(dinner film)`). Examples: - `subject:OneMCP Update` - `from:gduser1@workspacesamples.dev` - `to:gduser2@workspacesamples.dev AND newer_than:7d` - `project proposal has:attachment` - `is:unread` A space or a dash (`-`) separates numbers, while a dot (`.`) is treated as a decimal. For example, `01.2047-100` is considered two numbers: `01.2047` and `100`. To search for hyphenated or dotted identifiers (such as order numbers, tracking IDs, or invoice codes like `INV-12345`), enclose them in double quotes (e.g., `"INV-12345"` or `"01.2047-100"`) so the dash is not interpreted as a negation operator and exact phrase matching is preserved. Note: If we want to ensure all drafts for the query are returned, we can paginate the results by making repeated calls to the tool until the response contains an empty list of drafts.

view.description: Optional. Controls the fields populated for drafts in the draft list. Defaults to returning metadata only (`id`, `threadId`, `toRecipients`, `ccRecipients`, `bccRecipients`, `date`). Set to `DRAFT_VIEW_FULL` to include `subject` and `plaintextBody` content.
x-google-enum-descriptions: Unspecified view. Defaults to DRAFT_VIEW_METADATA_ONLY.
Returns metadata only (`id`, `threadId`, `toRecipients`, `ccRecipients`, `bccRecipients`, `date`) (if applicable); omits `subject` and `plaintextBody` content.
Returns full draft content, including `subject` and `plaintextBody` in addition to draft metadata (if applicable).

tools.name: get_draft
tools.title: Get draft email
tools.description:
Retrieves a specific draft email from the authenticated user's Gmail account by ID, including its `viewUrl` for viewing and editing in the Gmail Web UI.

The optional `messageFormat` parameter controls the format of the draft returned. By default (or with `PLAIN_TEXT`), it returns the plain text body without the HTML body. Use `MINIMAL` to return snippet and key headers, `METADATA_ONLY` to exclude snippet, subject, and body, `FULL_CONTENT` for the complete draft including the HTML body, or `RAW` for the raw MIME message content.

draftId.description: Required. The unique identifier of the draft to fetch.

messageFormat.description: Optional. Specifies the format of the draft returned. Defaults to `PLAIN_TEXT`.

Returns all message fields (`id`, `snippet`, `subject`, `sender`, `toRecipients`, `ccRecipients`, `bccRecipients`, `addressDisplayNames`, `date`, `labelIds`, `attachmentIds`, `plaintextBody`, `htmlBody`, `attachments`, `viewUrl`) if applicable.

Note: This tool does not support retrieving drafts. Any draft messages within a thread are omitted. To view drafts, use the `list_drafts` tool instead.

Use `FULL_CONTENT` only when the HTML body is needed. Use `MINIMAL` to include only subject and snippet (excluding body). Use `METADATA_ONLY` to include only basic metadata (message ID, thread ID, viewUrl, labels, timestamp, and size estimate).

tools.name: search_threads
tools.title: Search email threads
tools.description:
Lists email threads from the authenticated user's Gmail account.

This tool can filter threads based on a query string and supports pagination. It returns a list of threads, each with its thread `id`, `messageCount` (total messages in the thread), `viewUrl`, and a subset of up to 5 related messages (each with its own message `id`, `viewUrl`, `sender`, recipients, `date`, and `labelIds`). Use this tool to find thread `id`s matching a query before reading full threads or performing actions on matching emails or threads. The `view` parameter controls which additional fields are populated in the returned message subset. By default (or with `THREAD_VIEW_MINIMAL`), it includes `subject` and `snippet`. Use `THREAD_VIEW_METADATA_ONLY` to exclude `subject` and `snippet`, `THREAD_VIEW_SUMMARY` to return `THREAD_VIEW_MINIMAL` fields with only the most recent message per thread, or `THREAD_VIEW_IDS_ONLY` to return only `id` on each thread without fetching per-thread message metadata. Full message bodies, attachment metadata, and messages beyond the 5-message subset are not returned by this tool; use the 'get_thread' tool with a thread ID to retrieve all messages (and their message IDs) in a thread or to fetch full message bodies. Threads with excluded criteria may still appear in the results. This occurs because Gmail identifies matching messages first. For example, if you search for -is:starred, Gmail will find an entire thread if it contains at least one unstarred message, even if other emails in that same conversation are starred.

To list threads in a specific inbox category tab, use the `category:` operator with `primary`, `social`, `promotions`, `updates`, or `forums` (e.g. `in:inbox category:promotions`).

When filtering by date, `after:` and `before:` both evaluate against midnight (00:00:00) of the specified date (`after:` is inclusive, `before:` is exclusive). To search through a specific day D (or for a date range), set `before:` to the day after (e.g. `after:2026/02/01 before:2026/02/02` for Feb 1, or `after:2026/02/01 before:2026/02/06` for Feb 1–5).

When searching for numbers, a space or dash (`-`) separates numbers while a dot (`.`) is treated as a decimal (e.g., `01.2047-100` is parsed as two numbers: `01.2047` and `100`). To search for hyphenated or dotted identifiers (such as order numbers, tracking IDs, or invoice codes like `INV-12345`), enclose them in double quotes (e.g. "INV-12345" or "01.2047-100") so the dash is not interpreted as a negation operator.

Note: An empty JSON object `{}` represents zero matching items, not an error.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of threads to return. If unspecified, defaults to 20. The maximum allowed value is 50.

pageToken.description: Optional. Page token to retrieve a specific page of results in the list. Leave empty to fetch the first page. This is primarily used for pagination to continue fetching results from where the previous `SearchThreads` call left off, especially when the number of threads matching the query exceeds the `pageSize` limit.

tools.name: label_thread
tools.title: Add labels to thread
tools.description:
Adds labels to an entire thread in the authenticated user's Gmail account. This operation affects all messages currently in the thread and any future messages added to it.

If unsure of a user label's ID, use the `list_labels` tool first to discover available labels and their IDs. To move a thread to a different inbox category tab, add the target `CATEGORY_*` label (e.g. `CATEGORY_PERSONAL` for Primary); Gmail automatically removes the previous category. To move a thread to Trash or mark it as Spam, please use the `trash_thread` or `mark_thread_spam` tool instead.

labelIds.description: Required. The unique identifiers of the labels to add. Can be a system label ID (e.g., `INBOX`, `STARRED`, `UNREAD`, `IMPORTANT`) or a user-defined label ID. The tool accepts `labelIds` and not label names. Use the `list_labels` tool to get the corresponding label id to a display name for user-defined labels.

threadId.description: Required. The unique identifier of the thread to add labels to.

tools.name: unlabel_thread
tools.title: Remove labels from thread
tools.description:
Removes labels from an entire thread in the authenticated user's Gmail account. This operation affects all messages currently in the thread.

Use `unlabel_thread` when removing labels from an email or thread (such as marking it as read by removing `UNREAD`, archiving it by removing `INBOX`, or removing user-defined labels), even if the thread currently contains only 1 message. If unsure of a user label's ID, use the `list_labels` tool first.

labelIds.description: Required. The unique identifiers of the labels to remove. Can be a system label ID (e.g., `INBOX`, `TRASH`, `STARRED`, `UNREAD`, `IMPORTANT`) or a user-defined label ID. `SPAM` cannot be removed with this tool. The tool accepts `labelIds` and not label names. Use the `list_labels` tool to get the corresponding label id to a display name for user-defined labels.

threadId.description: Required. The unique identifier of the thread to remove labels from.

tools.title: Move thread to Trash
tools.description:
Moves an entire thread to the Trash (soft delete) in the authenticated user's Gmail account. This operation affects all messages currently in the thread.

This is the default tool (along with `trash_message`) when a user asks to 'delete', 'remove', or 'get rid of' an email or thread without explicitly requesting permanent, irreversible deletion. Use `trash_thread` when trashing a thread, even if it currently contains only 1 message. Trashing at the thread level ensures all current messages in the thread are moved to Trash.

threadId.description: Required. The ID of the thread to move to Trash.

tools.name: untrash_thread
tools.title: Remove thread from Trash
tools.description: Removes an entire thread from the Trash in the authenticated user's Gmail account. This does not return the thread to the Inbox; to move it to the Inbox, add the `INBOX` label separately.

threadId.description: Required. The ID of the thread to remove from Trash.

tools.name: mark_thread_spam
tools.title: Mark thread as Spam
tools.description:
Marks an entire thread as Spam in the authenticated user's Gmail account. This operation affects all messages currently in the thread.

Use `mark_thread_spam` when marking a thread as spam, even if it currently contains only 1 message. Marking spam at the thread level ensures all current messages in the thread are marked as Spam.

threadId.description: Required. The ID of the thread to mark as Spam.

tools.name: unmark_thread_spam
tools.title: Unmark thread as Spam
tools.description: Unmarks an entire thread as Spam in the authenticated user's Gmail account. This does not return the thread to the Inbox; to move it to the Inbox, add the `INBOX` label separately.

threadId.description: Required. The ID of the thread to unmark as Spam.

tools.name: list_labels
tools.title: List labels
tools.description:
Lists all labels available in the authenticated user's Gmail account. Use this tool to discover the `labelId` and display `name` of each label in `labels` before calling `label_thread`, `unlabel_thread`, `label_message`, or `unlabel_message`. Note: the system labels, `DRAFT` and `SENT`, cannot be set on messages and are read only.

Inbox category tabs are represented by system labels: `CATEGORY_PERSONAL` (Primary), `CATEGORY_SOCIAL` (Social), `CATEGORY_PROMOTIONS` (Promotions), `CATEGORY_UPDATES` (Updates), and `CATEGORY_FORUMS` (Forums). A message has at most one category: adding a category label moves the message to that tab and automatically removes its previous category, and removing a category label without adding another moves the message to Primary.

Note: An empty JSON object `{}` represents zero matching items, not an error.

tools.name: label_message
tools.title: Add labels to message
tools.description:
Adds one or more labels to a specific message in the authenticated user's Gmail account.

To find the message ID, use the `get_thread` tool. If unsure of a user label's ID, use the `list_labels` tool first to discover available labels and their IDs.
To move a message to a different inbox category tab, add the target `CATEGORY_*` label (e.g. `CATEGORY_PERSONAL` for Primary); Gmail automatically removes the previous category.
To move a specific message to Trash or mark it as Spam, please use the `trash_message` or `mark_message_spam` tool instead.

labelIds.description: Required. The IDs of the labels to add. Can be a system label ID (e.g., `INBOX`, `STARRED`, `UNREAD`, `IMPORTANT`) or a user-defined label ID. The tool accepts `labelIds` and not label names. Use the `list_labels` tool to get the corresponding label id to a display name for user-defined labels.

messageId.description: Required. The ID of the message to add the labels to.

tools.name: update_message_labels
tools.title: Modify message labels
tools.description:
Atomically adds and/or removes labels from a specific message in the authenticated user's Gmail account.

Requires at least one of `addLabelIds` or `removeLabelIds` to be provided. Moving an email between labels can be accomplished in a single call by specifying the target label in `addLabelIds` and the current label in `removeLabelIds`.
For inbox category tabs, adding the target `CATEGORY_*` label (e.g. `CATEGORY_PERSONAL` for Primary) is sufficient; Gmail automatically removes the previous category.

addLabelIds.description: Optional. The IDs of the labels to add. Can be a system label ID (e.g., `INBOX`, `STARRED`, `UNREAD`, `IMPORTANT`) or a user-defined label ID.

messageId.description: Required. The ID of the message to modify labels for.

removeLabelIds.description: Optional. The IDs of the labels to remove. Can be a system label ID or a user-defined label ID.

tools.name: unlabel_message
tools.title: Remove labels from message
tools.description: Removes one or more labels from a specific message in the authenticated user's Gmail account. To find the message ID, use the `get_thread` tool. If unsure of a user label's ID, use the `list_labels` tool first to discover available labels and their IDs.

labelIds.description: Required. The IDs of the labels to remove. Can be a system label ID (e.g., `INBOX`, `TRASH`, `STARRED`, `UNREAD`, `IMPORTANT`) or a user-defined label ID. `SPAM` cannot be removed with this tool. The tool accepts `labelIds` and not label names. Use the `list_labels` tool to get the corresponding label id to a display name for user-defined labels.

messageId.description: Required. The ID of the message to remove the labels from.

tools.name: apply_sensitive_message_label
tools.title: Apply sensitive label (Trash or Spam) to message
tools.description:
Prefer `trash_message` or `mark_message_spam` instead.

Adds a sensitive label (Trash or Spam) to a single message in the authenticated user's Gmail account.

Use `apply_sensitive_message_label` when applying Trash or Spam to exactly 1 message. If the message belongs to a thread that should be labeled as a whole, prefer `trash_thread` or `mark_thread_spam`.

To find the message ID, use the `get_thread` tool. To find the draft message ID, use tools like `list_drafts`.

tools.name: copy_file

tools.description:
Call this tool to copy an existing File in Google Drive.
The tool allows specifying a new title and a parent folder for the copy.
If the title is not specified, the copy title will be 'Copy of {original title}'.
If the parent folder is not specified, the copy will be created in the same folder as the original file, unless the requesting user does not have write access to that folder, in which case the copy will be created in the user's root folder.
Pregenerated file IDs (`pregeneratedId`, obtained from `generate_ids`) are supported when copying non-Google Workspace files.
Returns the newly created File object upon successful copying.

parentId.description: The parent id of the newly created file. If empty, the file will be created with the same parent as the original file.

title.description: The title of the newly created file. If empty, the title will be 'Copy of {original file title}'.

tools.name: create_file
tools.title: Create file
tools.description:
Call this tool to create or upload a File to Google Drive.

If uploading content, prefer `textContent` for text content. For non-UTF8 contents, use the `base64Content` field and base64 encode the data to set on that field.

Returns a single File object upon successful creation.

The following Google first-party mime types can be created without providing content:

 - `application/vnd.google-apps.document` 
 - `application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet` 
 - `application/vnd.google-apps.presentation` 

Folders can be created by setting the mime type to `application/vnd.google-apps.folder`.

When uploading content, the `contentMimeType` field is required and should match the type of the content being uploaded.

By default, supported content will be converted to Google first-party mime types.

To disable conversions for first-party mime types, set `disableConversionToGoogleType` to true.

Pregenerated file IDs (`pregeneratedId`, obtained from `generate_ids`) are supported for non-Google Workspace files and folders (`application/vnd.google-apps.folder`). When uploading content with `pregeneratedId`, `disableConversionToGoogleType` must be set to true.

base64Content.description: Optional. The base64 encoded content to upload. It's an error to set this and `textContent`.

content.description: Deprecated: Use `base64Content` or `textContent` instead. The content of the file encoded as base64. The content field should always be base64 encoded regardless of the mime type of the file.

contentMimeType.description: The mime type of the content being uploaded. Required when any type of content is provided.

disableConversionToGoogleType.description: Set to true to retain the passed in content mime type and not convert to a Google type. For example, without this a `text/plain` content mime type will be converted to to `application/vnd.google-apps.document`. Has no effect for types that do not have a Google equivalent.

inheritedPermissionsDisabled.description: Set to true to disable inherited permissions on the created folder, restricting access to only users with direct permissions on the folder.

mimeType.description: Deprecated: DO NOT USE!! Set `contentMimeType` instead.

parentId.description: The parent id of the file.

pregeneratedId.description: Optional. The pregenerated id of the file to create, obtained from the `generate_ids` tool. Supported for binary/blob files and folders (`application/vnd.google-apps.folder`); not supported for native Google Workspace document types. When uploading content with a pregenerated id, `disableConversionToGoogleType` must be set to true.

textContent.description: Optional. The (UTF-8) text content to upload. It's an error to set this and `base64Content`.

title.description: Required. The title of the file.

tools.name: download_file_content
tools.title: Download file content
tools.description:
Call this tool to download the content of a Drive file as a base64 encoded string.

If the file is a Google Drive first-party mime type, the `exportMimeType` field specifies the desired export mime type. When the field is unset, defaults to plain text types (e.g. `text/plain`, `text/csv`).

If the file is not found, try using other tools like `search_files` to find the file the user is requesting.

If the user wants a natural language representation of their Drive content, use the `read_file_content` tool (`read_file_content` should be smaller and easier to parse).

inputSchema.description: Defines a request to download a file's content.

exportMimeType.description: Optional. For Google native files, the MIME type to export the file to, ignored otherwise. Defaults to text if not specified.

fileId.description: Required. The ID of the file to retrieve.

revisionId.description: Optional. The revision id for the version of the file to download. If not specified, the latest revision will be downloaded.

tools.name: list_recent_files
tools.title: List recent files
tools.description:
Call this tool to find recent files for a user specified a sort order. Default sort order is `recency` if orderBy is not set or set to an unsupported value.

Context window token management can be tuned via `snippetVerbosity` (default is `SnippetVerbosity.DETAILED`) or if only metadata is needed, use `excludeContentSnippets`.

Supported sort orders are:

 - `recency`: The most recent timestamp from the file's date-time fields.
 - `lastModified`: The last time the file was modified by anyone.
 - `lastModifiedByMe`: The last time the file was modified by the user.

The default page size is 10. Utilize `nextPageToken` to paginate through the results.

tools.name: read_file_content
tools.title: Read file content
tools.description:
Call this tool to fetch a natural language representation of a known Drive file, and if specified, its comments.

REQUIREMENTS & WORKFLOW:
 - `fileId` is required. You MUST pass an exact Drive file ID returned by a previous discovery tool (`search_files` or `list_recent_files`) or provided explicitly in the user prompt.
 - If given a file title, name, or topic without an explicit `fileId`, you MUST FIRST call `search_files` to find the file and retrieve its `fileId` before invoking this tool.
 - Set `includeComments` to `true` when the user asks about comments, feedback, action items, open questions, or discussion threads on the file, or before replying to or resolving a comment.

The file content may be incomplete for very large files. The text representation will change over time, so don't make assumptions about the particular format of the text returned by this tool. If supported and specified, comment tags will be included in the content.

Supported Mime Types:

 - `application/vnd.google-apps.document` (supports comments)
 - `application/vnd.google-apps.presentation` (supports comments)
 - `application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet` (supports comments)
 - `application/pdf` 
 - `application/msword` 
 - `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document` 
 - `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet` 
 - `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation` 
 - `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.spreadsheet` 
 - `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.presentation` 
 - `application/x-vnd.oasis.opendocument.text` 
 - `image/png` 
 - `image/jpeg` 
 - `image/jpg` 
 - `text/*` 
 - `video/*` (when a transcript is available)

If the file is not found, try using other tools like `search_files` to find the file the user is requesting using keywords.

inputSchema.description: Request to read file content with support for fetching comments.

fileId.description: Required. The ID of the file to retrieve.

includeComments.description: Whether to include comments in the response. Set to true when the user asks about comments, feedback, action items, open questions, or discussion threads on the file, or before replying to or resolving a comment. Comments will be inlined in the text content of the file with a mapping to the comment threads. Note: Comments are only supported for Google Docs, Slides, and Sheets.

tools.name: search_files
tools.title: Search files
tools.description:
Search for Drive files using a structured query (syntax: `query_term operator values`). Only terms in this list are supported.
Combine clauses with `and`, `or`, `not`, and parentheses. String values must be single-quoted; escape embedded quotes as `\'`.
Context window token management can be tuned via `snippetVerbosity` (default is `SnippetVerbosity.DETAILED`) or if only metadata is needed, use `excludeContentSnippets`.
To display a folder hierarchy, directory tree structure, or recursive directory and file counts, prefer `get_folder_tree` (when available) over emulating tree traversal with `search_files`; use `search_files` first only if you need to look up a named folder's ID.

Use `title contains` instead of `title =` when searching by file or folder name, unless the user explicitly asks for an exact full-title match. Do NOT include document type terms (e.g., 'presentation', 'slides', 'deck', 'document', 'doc', 'spreadsheet', 'sheet', 'pdf', 'folder', 'project') inside `title` or `fullText` clauses. Separate title keywords from file type terms and map them to `mimeType` clauses in the query.

Where a folder ID is expected (`parentId`, `ancestors`), `'root'` means the user's "My Drive".

Query terms & operators:

 - `title` (ops: contains, =, !=) — file title
 - `fullText` (ops: contains) — title or body text
 - `mimeType` (ops: contains, =, !=) — MIME type
 - `modifiedTime`, `viewedByMeTime`, `createdTime` (ops: `<=`, `<`, `=`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`). Use RFC 3339 UTC, e.g., `2012-06-04T12:00:00-08:00`. Date types not comparable.
 - `parentId` (ops: `=`, `!=`). Direct children only.
 - `ancestors` (use `'<folderId>' in ancestors`). Files anywhere under the folder, including nested subfolders. Recently moved files may take a short time to appear.
 - `owner` (ops: `=`, `!=`). Use `'me'` for the requesting user.
 - `readers`, `writers` (use `'me' in readers` or `'user@example.com' in writers`). 
 - `creator` (ops: `=`, `!=`). `'me'` or an email — who created the file.
 - `sharedFrom` (ops: `=`, `!=`). An email — who shared the file with the user.
 - `sharedTo` (ops: `=`, `!=`). An email — who the user shared the file with.
 - `visibility` (ops: `=`, `!=`): `'anyoneWithLink'`, `'anyoneCanFind'`, `'anyone'`, `'domainWithLink'`, `'domainCanFind'`, `'domain'`, `'limited'` (not shared via link, domain or publicly), `'external'` (shared with people outside the user's organization).
 - `sharedWithMe`, `starred` (ops: `=`, `!=`). `true` or `false`.
 - `folderProperties` (use `'value' in folderProperties`): `'syncedComputer'` (synced computer), `'syncFolder'` (synced folder).
 - `followUp` (ops: `=`, `!=`): `'assignedcomments'` (aliases `'todos'`, `'actionitems'`), `'suggestions'`, `'any'` — files with open follow-ups for the user.
 - `trashed` (ops: `=`, `!=`). `true` or `false` (default `false`).

Other operators: `and`, `or`, `not`, `in`.

Examples:

 - `title contains 'hello' and title contains 'goodbye'`
 - `modifiedTime > '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z' and (mimeType contains 'image/' or mimeType contains 'video/')`
 - `mimeType = 'application/vnd.google-apps.project'` (for Drive projects)
 - `parentId = '1234567'` (direct children of a folder)
 - `'1234567' in ancestors and mimeType = 'application/pdf'` (PDFs anywhere under a folder)
 - `fullText contains 'hello'`
 - `owner = 'test@example.org'`
 - `sharedWithMe = true`
 - `starred = true`
 - `owner = 'me'` (for files owned by the user)
 - `'colleague@example.org' in writers and sharedFrom = 'colleague@example.org'`
 - `owner = 'me' and visibility = 'anyone'` (user's files shared publicly or by link)
 - `'syncedComputer' in folderProperties`

Use `nextPageToken` to paginate. Duplicate results can occur across page boundaries. An empty response means no more results.

excludeContentSnippets.description: If `true`, the content snippet will be excluded from the response. Must not be set to `true` if `snippetVerbosity` is specified.

includeExternalityState.description: Optional. When true, also returns `externality_state` for each file. Defaults to `false`.

includeRichMetadata.description: Optional. When true, also returns `owner_name`, `last_modifying_user_name`, `last_modifying_user_email`, `visibility`, and `last_commented_time`. Defaults to `false`.

orderBy.description: Optional. The sort order for the search results. Specifies a single sort clause with syntax `<field> [asc|desc]`. Supported fields: - `modifiedTime` (defaults to `desc`) - `viewedByMeTime` (defaults to `desc`) Examples: `modifiedTime desc`, `viewedByMeTime`. If omitted or empty, results are ordered by relevance descending. Unsupported fields or invalid directions return an error.

pageSize.description: The maximum number of files to return in each page.

pageToken.description: The page token to use for pagination.

snippetVerbosity.description: Optional. Set to specify how verbose the snippets should be. Defaults to `DETAILED` if not set. Must not be set if `excludeContentSnippets` is `true`.

The verbosity is greatly increased, limited by the overall response size.

tools.name: upload_file_revision
tools.title: Upload file revision
tools.description:
Call this tool to upload a new content revision for an existing blob file in Google Drive.

Prefer `textContent` for UTF-8 text content. For binary or non-UTF8 contents, use the `base64Content` field and base64 encode the data.

The `contentMimeType` field is required and should match the type of the content being uploaded.

If the file is not found, try using other tools like `search_files` to find the file the user is attempting to update.

inputSchema.description: Request to upload a new revision for a blob file.

base64Content.description: Optional base64-encoded binary content to upload. Either base64Content or textContent must be set, but not both.

contentMimeType.description: Required. The MIME type of the content to upload.

etag.description: Optional. Opaque version token used for optimistic concurrency control (preventing concurrent edit conflicts). If set, the upload fails with FAILED_PRECONDITION if the file has been modified since the etag was returned. OMIT this field if you have not previously retrieved the file. Never fabricate or manually format an etag value. ONLY pass the exact, unaltered string previously received in `File.etag` or `Revision.file_etag` from a prior read or write operation.

fileId.description: Required. The ID of the file to update with a new revision.

textContent.description: Optional UTF-8 text content to upload. Either base64Content or textContent must be set, but not both.
